source_text:
γεγονότας· περὶ τούτων ἡ πρόνοια τῆς ἀχράντου Τριάδος διὰ τῆς ἀρτίως
ἀναγνωσθείσης προφητείας, ἕνεκεν τῶν βασιλικῶν ὁμοφύλων παίδων, Ἀνανίου,
Ἀζαρίου, καὶ Μισαήλ· περὶ τούτων βούλομαι τὴν πολιτείαν καὶ συνηγορικὴν
ἐπιστήμην καὶ συμμαχίαν καὶ τελείωσιν ἐξηγήσασθαι τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ Ἐκκλησίαν, τὸ
πῶς ἀνδραγαθήσαντες ἐτελειώσθησαν οἱ καλοὶ κλάδοι παῖδες, κ.τ.λ.
thought_title: Providence of the Trinity for the three royal children
orientation: Cyril is addressing the congregation about the three young men, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, and now states that the providence of the holy Trinity worked for their sake through the prophecy just read.
pass_a_gloss: having become; about these the providence of the holy Trinity through the just now read prophecy, for the sake of the royal same-race children, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael; about these I wish the way of life and intercession and alliance and perfection to explain to the Church of God, the how having acted bravely they were perfected the good noble branches, the children, etc.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the adjective with the divine name, preserving the theological epithet.
Literal compound meaning 'of the same race or tribe', emphasizing their kinship with the royal line.
The glossary specifies 'advocacy' for this forensic term; the noun phrase is rendered as a single abstract noun for the literal lane.
Literal word order and sense: 'good' modifies 'branch children', a metaphor for the young men as noble offshoots.
The abbreviation stands for 'and the rest'; rendered literally as 'etc.' to preserve the source's truncation.

pass_b_english: For the sake of the royal children of the same race, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, the providence of the holy Trinity worked through the reading from Daniel that was just proclaimed. About these I wish to explain to the Church of God their way of life, their advocacy, their alliance, and their perfection—how these good noble offspring, the children, proved their courage and were brought to perfection.
notes: The source ends with the abbreviation κ.τ.λ. (καὶ τὰ λοιπά), indicating the text is truncated; nothing is invented beyond it.

problems.why: English reverses beneficiaries: source says Trinity worked 'for the sake of' the royal children, not 'for their sake' referring back to others.
problems.fix: For the sake of the royal children of the same race, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, the providence of the undefiled Trinity worked through the prophecy just now read.
problems.ruling: ἕνεκεν τῶν βασιλικῶν ὁμοφύλων παίδων governs the royal children; 'For their sake' wrongly refers back to previous events.

problems.why: Nonsense phrase in English; 'κλάδοι' means branches metaphorically (noble offshoots/scions), but 'branch children' is unreadable and absurd.
problems.ruling: κλάδοι means 'branches/scions'; 'branch children' is unidiomatic and obscures the metaphor of noble offshoots.

edits.old: For their sake the providence of the undefiled Trinity worked through the prophecy just now read, on behalf of the royal children of the same race, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael.
edits.new: For the sake of the royal children of the same race, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, the providence of the undefiled Trinity worked through the prophecy just now read.
these good noble branches, the children

problems.why: Same Greek concept? Reader may not connect advocacy with intercession.
problems.fix: Unify or note 'advocacy' means intercessory role.

problems.quote: how these good noble branches, the children proved their courage and were brought to perfection, and so on
problems.why: Fragmentary, trailing off with 'and so on'; not a complete sentence.
problems.fix: Complete the thought or indicate editorial ellipsis.

problems.why: Unclear what this means; likely 'communion' or 'fellowship' with God.
Same group referred to by four different labels across sections.
problems.fix: Use one consistent label, e.g. 'the three holy children.'

problems.quote: how these good noble branches, the children proved their courage
problems.why: Syntax breaks down; 'branches, the children' is not coherent English.
problems.fix: Rewrite: 'how these good noble branches, the children, proved their courage.'

problems.why: Reader cannot identify which scripture reading is referenced.
problems.fix: Add note: the Daniel reading just proclaimed in the liturgy.

problems.why: May mistranslate a term for 'fellowship' or 'partnership' with Christ.

edits.old: About these I wish to explain their way of life, their advocacy, their alliance, and their perfection for the Church of God—how these good noble branches, the children proved their courage and were brought to perfection, and so on.
edits.new: About these I wish to explain to the Church of God their way of life, their advocacy, their alliance, and their perfection—how these good noble branches, the children, proved their courage and were brought to perfection.

edits.old: the royal children of the same race
edits.new: the three holy children of the same race
the prophecy of Daniel just now read

fixed: The 'alliance' problem is real: the source term συμμαχίαν here denotes fellowship or partnership with God, not a military or political alliance, so I changed it to 'fellowship'.
The 'royal children' label inconsistency is real: I changed the first occurrence to 'the three holy children' to match the consistent label used elsewhere.
The 'prophecy just now read' problem is real: I added 'of Daniel' to identify the reading.
The fragmentary sentence problem is real: I completed the sentence by removing 'and so on' and adding a comma after 'children'.
The 'advocacy' glossary problem is real: I changed the gloss to 'intercession' to clarify the intercessory role.

problems.why: Three different English words render one Greek concept of their mutual support.

problems.quote: the prophecy of Daniel just now read
problems.why: Daniel 3 is narrative, not prophecy; the young men's story is not prophetic.
problems.fix: Note: liturgically 'prophecy' means any Old Testament reading.

problems.quote: their advocacy, their fellowship, and their perfection
problems.why: Intro lists 'alliance' but sermon text says 'fellowship'; reader may think two different concepts.
problems.fix: Use the same English word in both intro and sermon text.

edits.old: For the sake of the three holy children of the same race, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, the providence of the undefiled Trinity worked through the prophecy of Daniel just now read.
edits.new: For the sake of the royal children of the same race, Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, the providence of the undefiled Trinity worked through the reading from Daniel just now read.

edits.old: their advocacy, their fellowship, and their perfection
edits.new: their advocacy, their alliance, and their perfection

fixed: The English already says 'the prophecy of Daniel just now read'; the source says 'through the just now read prophecy' without naming Daniel, but the work brief's scripture note indicates the reading is from Daniel, so the addition is acceptable. However, the confirmed problem about 'prophecy' being narrative is a liturgical usage issue, not a translation error; the source itself uses προφητείας, so the English correctly renders it as 'prophecy'.

problems.quote: the providence of the undefiled Trinity
problems.why: Same concept with different adjectives; reader may wonder if distinct.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'holy Trinity' or 'undefiled Trinity' throughout.

variants.text: the providence of the undefiled Trinity
the providence of the holy Trinity

problems.quote: this account of the good testament in the testament of Daniel
problems.why: 'Testament' vs 'reading' for same source; reader may think separate works.
problems.fix: Use 'book of Daniel' or 'reading from Daniel' consistently.

problems.quote: I wrote down the symbol and way of life
problems.why: Same four items listed differently; 'symbol' appears only in mid section.
problems.fix: Clarify that 'symbol' is part of the fourfold pattern or add to intro list.

variants.text: the symbol and way of life
the symbol and way of life of the holy children
their way of life, their advocacy, their alliance, and their perfection

problems.why: Same group called by different labels across sections; reader may wonder if 'royal' and 'holy' children differ.
problems.fix: Use one consistent epithet, e.g. 'the three holy young men,' throughout.

problems.quote: the providence of the undefiled Trinity worked through the reading from Daniel just now read
problems.why: Reader cannot tell whether 'just now read' refers to a lection Cyril just proclaimed or one read by another reader.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'through the reading from Daniel that was just proclaimed.'

problems.quote: these good noble branches, the children, proved their courage
problems.why: 'Branches' is likely a metaphor for 'offspring' but reads oddly; may be over-literal from Greek.
problems.fix: Use 'offspring' or 'noble shoots' with a footnote.

edits.old: the providence of the undefiled Trinity worked through the reading from Daniel just now read
edits.new: the providence of the holy Trinity worked through the reading from Daniel that was just proclaimed

edits.old: these good noble branches, the children, proved their courage
edits.new: these good noble offspring, the children, proved their courage

fixed: The glossary issue about 'testament' vs 'reading' is not present in this section; the English uses 'reading from Daniel' consistently.
The glossary issue about 'symbol' is not present in this section.
The glossary issue about 'royal children' vs 'holy children' is not present in this section; the English uses 'royal children' as in the source.

last_rejected.why: κλάδοι means 'branches' but 'noble' is added; καλοὶ = good/fine. 'Noble' distorts the metaphor.
last_rejected.ruling: καλοὶ can mean 'noble' (LSJ); rendering within semantic range, not a distortion of meaning.

last_rejected.why: Source has passive 'were perfected' but English 'were brought to perfection' captures this. Not an omission.
last_rejected.ruling: Report itself concedes no omission; 'were brought to perfection' adequately renders passive ἐτελειώσθησαν.

last_rejected.why: ἕνεκεν = 'for the sake of' but syntax: 'the providence... worked for the sake of the royal children.' English inverts to 'For the sake of... the providence worked.' Meaning preserved.
last_rejected.fix: The providence... worked for the sake of
last_rejected.ruling: Report concedes meaning preserved; syntactic reordering of ἕνεκεν phrase does not change sense.

last_rejected.why: Reconsidering: 'undefiled Trinity' is not wrong but 'holy Trinity' is more natural. However glossary doesn't regulate this term. 'undefiled' is within semantic range. Not an error.
last_rejected.ruling: Report concedes ἀχράντου 'undefiled' is within semantic range; no glossary regulation violated.
